title: 1973 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Let \([t]\) denote the greatest integer not exceeding \(t,\) where \(t\ge0,\) and \[ \begin{aligned} S=\{(x,y):{}&(x-T)^2+y^2\\ &\le T^2\},\\ T&=t-[t]. \end{aligned} \] Then we have

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: the point \((0,0)\) does not belong to \(S\) for any \(t\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: \(S\) is contained in the first quadrant for all \(t\ge5\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the center of \(S\) for any \(t\) is on the line \(y=x\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: none of the other statements is true

solutions.text:
The fractional part satisfies \(0\le T\lt1.\) The set \(S\) is the closed disk centered at \((T,0)\) with radius \(T.\) Its area is \[ \pi T^2, \] so \(0\le\operatorname{Area}S\lt\pi,\) which in particular gives \(0\le\operatorname{Area}S\le\pi.\) The origin lies on every such disk, the disk extends below the \(x\)-axis when \(T\gt0,\) and its center is generally not on \(y=x.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Recognize \(T=t-[t]\) as the fractional part of \(t\)
Interpret the equation for \(S\) as a disk and identify its center and radius
